extDescription.message: Manage local HTML and Claude artifact tabs in one side panel. No duplicate tabs, no stolen focus.

agentPrompt.message:
Set up Artifact Dock (https://github.com/woorichicken/artifact-dock) on this Mac. The Chrome extension is already installed. Follow these steps, check the result of each one, and give me a summary at the end.

1. Prerequisites: confirm this is macOS and that `git` and `python3` are available.
2. Install: if `~/artifact-dock` doesn't exist, run `git clone https://github.com/woorichicken/artifact-dock.git ~/artifact-dock`; otherwise `git -C ~/artifact-dock pull --ff-only`. Then run `~/artifact-dock/install.sh`. It registers the native host and installs `artifact-open` and an `open` wrapper into `~/.local/bin`. If it stops because a different `open` already exists there, don't overwrite it — tell me.
3. Route `open` through Artifact Dock: in the shell config (`~/.zshrc` for zsh), make sure `~/.local/bin` comes before `/usr/bin` in PATH. Skip if it already does; if you add a line, tell me exactly what you added. It's an executable wrapper, not a shell function or alias, so `open file.html` from agents, scripts, and Node also goes through Artifact Dock into a background tab. Non-HTML files are passed to the original `open` unchanged.
4. Verify: in a new shell, check that `command -v open` is `~/.local/bin/open` and `artifact-open --status` reports the extension as alive. If it isn't connected, ask me to turn the extension off and on in Chrome. Finally, open a temporary HTML file with `open` and ask me to confirm it opened in a background tab without covering what I was looking at.
5. From now on: open HTML output with `artifact-open <file>` (or `open <file>`). If the command fails, do not work around it with `/usr/bin/open`, AppleScript, or anything else — tell me and include the file path.

welcomeLead.message: Keeps agent-made HTML reports to one tab per document, without stealing your focus. Each step below checks itself off when it's done.

step1Desc.message: Open the side panel from the toolbar icon or ⌘⇧U. Pin it to the toolbar to find it easily.

step2Desc.message: Needed for local HTML (file://). Turn on "Allow access to file URLs" on the extension's details page.

step3Desc.message: Run this once in the terminal to install the artifact-open command and its connector — or hand it to your agent with the prompt in step 4. This step updates on its own a few seconds after install.

step3Hint.message: Already installed but still waiting? Turn the extension off and on in chrome://extensions.

step4Title.message: Let your agent set it up

step4Desc.message: Paste this prompt into a Claude Code or Codex chat. Your agent installs the CLI, routes `open` through Artifact Dock (shell PATH setup), checks the connection, and reports back.

allReady.message: All set — reports your agent opens will now gather in the side panel.

notReady.message: Finish the remaining steps and this will show as ready.

privacyNote.message: This extension collects no data and sends nothing off your device.

optLead.message: Groups local HTML and artifact tabs. Changes are saved instantly.

optDedupeDesc.message: Opening a document that's already open reuses its tab and closes the new one.

optMatch.message: What counts as the same document

optMatchDesc.message: Full path merges only the same file · File name only also merges /a/report.html and /b/report.html · Document title merges different files with the same <title> (before the title loads the path is used, so it mostly helps with the Tidy up button)

optReloadDesc.message: On by default, since the agent has probably rewritten the file.

optFocusGuard.message: Don't focus tabs opened from outside

optFocusGuardDesc.message: If a tab was opened from the terminal, switches back to the tab you were on. Links opened from a page are left alone.

optAutoGroup.message: Put artifact tabs in a group

optAutoGroupDesc.message: They sit together in the tab bar and take less space.

optViewMode.message: When viewing from the side panel

optViewModeDesc.message: Pull out one moves only that tab out of the group; the rest stay collapsed (recommended) · Expand group activates it normally; the group expands and collapses again when you leave

optCollapseDesc.message: Turn on to save tab bar space. Works best when you pick documents from the side panel.

optSweepOnStart.message: Tidy up duplicates when the browser starts

optSweepOnStartDesc.message: When off, tidying happens only when you click Tidy up in the side panel.

optMaxTabsDesc.message: 0 means no limit. Beyond it, the least recently viewed close first — they stay in the list and reopen with one click (pinned and current tabs are kept).

optTrackClaudeDesc.message: When off, only local file:// HTML is managed.

missingTitle.message: The file was deleted — Tidy up removes it from the list

toastMissing.message: This file was deleted, so it can't be opened. Tidy up removes it from the list

optAutoPruneMissingDesc.message: Files that disappear on reboot or cleanup (like /tmp) are removed from Recently closed automatically (once an hour). Open tabs close only when you click Tidy up. Needs the CLI (install.sh) 0.5.0 or later.

optCleanupDaysDesc.message: 0 turns it off. Documents not reopened or viewed for N days are closed and removed from the list (once an hour). Pinned (📌) documents and the tab you're viewing stay.
